title: Abstract Algebra I
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 300L Abstract Algebra I curriculum, focused on group theory: group axioms, subgroups, cyclic groups, permutation groups, cosets, Lagrange's Theorem, normal subgroups, quotient groups, and group homomorphisms/isomorphisms.

questions.question: A group (G, *) must satisfy which of the following axioms?
options: Closure, associativity, existence of identity, and existence of inverses
questions.correct_answer: Closure, associativity, existence of identity, and existence of inverses
questions.explanation: These four axioms define a group; commutativity is an additional property that makes a group abelian, but is not required in general.

questions.question: The order of a finite group G is:
options: The number of elements in G
The number of subgroups of G
questions.correct_answer: The number of elements in G
questions.explanation: The order |G| simply counts the elements in the group.

questions.question: A nonempty subset H of a group G is a subgroup of G if and only if:
options: H is closed under the group operation and taking inverses (equivalently ab⁻¹ ∈ H for all a, b ∈ H)
H contains only the identity element
H has the same number of elements as G
H is any arbitrary subset of G
questions.correct_answer: H is closed under the group operation and taking inverses (equivalently ab⁻¹ ∈ H for all a, b ∈ H)
questions.explanation: The subgroup test requires closure under the operation and under inverses; associativity is inherited automatically from G.

questions.question: Every group G has at least which two subgroups (the trivial subgroups)?
questions.correct_answer: {e} and G itself
questions.explanation: The identity subgroup {e} and the whole group G are always subgroups of G, referred to as the trivial subgroups.

questions.question: A group G is called cyclic if:
options: There exists an element g ∈ G such that every element of G is a power of g
questions.correct_answer: There exists an element g ∈ G such that every element of G is a power of g
questions.explanation: A cyclic group is generated by a single element g, meaning G = {g^n : n ∈ ℤ}.

questions.question: The order of an element g in a group G is defined as:
options: The smallest positive integer n such that g^n = e
The order of the group G
The number of subgroups generated by g
questions.correct_answer: The smallest positive integer n such that g^n = e
questions.explanation: The order of an element is the least positive n for which repeated application of the operation returns the identity; if no such n exists, the element has infinite order.

questions.question: Every cyclic group is necessarily:
questions.correct_answer: Abelian
questions.explanation: Since all elements of a cyclic group are powers of a single generator, and powers of the same element commute, every cyclic group is abelian.

questions.question: The symmetric group Sn consists of:
options: All permutations of n distinct objects, under composition
All symmetric matrices of size n
questions.correct_answer: All permutations of n distinct objects, under composition
questions.explanation: Sn is the group of all bijections (permutations) of the set {1, 2, ..., n}, with the group operation being function composition.

questions.question: What is the order of the symmetric group S4?
questions.explanation: The order of Sn is n!, so |S4| = 4! = 24.

questions.question: A transposition in a permutation group is:
options: A permutation that swaps two elements and leaves all others fixed
A permutation with no fixed points
questions.correct_answer: A permutation that swaps two elements and leaves all others fixed
questions.explanation: A transposition is the simplest nontrivial permutation, exchanging exactly two elements.

questions.question: The symmetric group S3 (order 6) is an example of a group that is:
questions.correct_answer: Non-abelian
questions.explanation: S3 is the smallest non-abelian group; composing two transpositions in different orders gives different results.

questions.question: For a subgroup H of a group G and an element a ∈ G, the left coset aH is defined as:
questions.correct_answer: {ah : h ∈ H}
questions.explanation: The left coset aH consists of all products of a with elements of H, in that order.

questions.question: Lagrange's Theorem states that for a finite group G and subgroup H:
options: The order of H divides the order of G
The order of G divides the order of H
H and G have the same order
H must be a normal subgroup of G
questions.correct_answer: The order of H divides the order of G
questions.explanation: Lagrange's Theorem is a cornerstone result: |H| always divides |G| for any subgroup H of a finite group G.

questions.question: By a corollary of Lagrange's Theorem, the order of any element g in a finite group G:
questions.correct_answer: Divides the order of G
questions.explanation: Since the cyclic subgroup generated by g has order equal to the order of g, and this must divide |G| by Lagrange's Theorem.

questions.question: A group of prime order p must be:
questions.correct_answer: Cyclic (and hence abelian)
questions.explanation: By Lagrange's Theorem, any non-identity element generates a subgroup whose order divides p, so it must have order p, meaning the element generates the whole group, making it cyclic.

questions.question: A subgroup N of G is called a normal subgroup if:
options: gNg⁻¹ = N for every g ∈ G
N is always the whole group G
questions.correct_answer: gNg⁻¹ = N for every g ∈ G
questions.explanation: Normality requires that N is invariant under conjugation by every element of G, i.e. left and right cosets of N coincide.

questions.question: In an abelian group, every subgroup is:
questions.correct_answer: Normal
questions.explanation: Since gh = hg for all elements in an abelian group, every subgroup automatically satisfies gNg⁻¹ = N, making it normal.

questions.question: Given a normal subgroup N of G, the quotient group G/N consists of:
options: The set of cosets of N in G, with coset multiplication as the operation
The elements of G not in N
The set of all subgroups of G
questions.correct_answer: The set of cosets of N in G, with coset multiplication as the operation
questions.explanation: The quotient group's elements are the cosets gN, and (aN)(bN) = (ab)N defines a well-defined group operation precisely because N is normal.

questions.question: A function f: G → H between two groups is called a group homomorphism if:
options: f(ab) = f(a)f(b) for all a, b ∈ G
f(a) = f(b) for all a, b
questions.correct_answer: f(ab) = f(a)f(b) for all a, b ∈ G
questions.explanation: A homomorphism preserves the group operation: applying the operation before or after mapping gives the same result.

questions.question: The kernel of a group homomorphism f: G → H is:
options: {g ∈ G : f(g) = eH}, and it is always a normal subgroup of G
The image of f in H
questions.correct_answer: {g ∈ G : f(g) = eH}, and it is always a normal subgroup of G
questions.explanation: The kernel consists of all elements mapping to the identity in H, and it is always a normal subgroup of the domain G.

questions.question: A group homomorphism f: G → H is injective if and only if:
options: H is a subgroup of G
questions.correct_answer: ker(f) = {e}
questions.explanation: A homomorphism is injective precisely when its kernel is trivial, containing only the identity element.

questions.question: A bijective group homomorphism f: G → H is called a(n):
questions.correct_answer: Isomorphism
questions.explanation: An isomorphism is a homomorphism that is also a bijection, indicating G and H have identical structure.

questions.question: If two groups G and H are isomorphic, this means:
options: They have identical algebraic structure, differing only in the labeling of elements
They have the same number of subgroups but different orders
One is a subgroup of the other
questions.correct_answer: They have identical algebraic structure, differing only in the labeling of elements
questions.explanation: Isomorphic groups are structurally indistinguishable as groups — any group-theoretic property of one holds for the other.

questions.question: The First Isomorphism Theorem states that for a homomorphism f: G → H:
options: G/ker(f) is isomorphic to the image of f
G is isomorphic to H always
questions.correct_answer: G/ker(f) is isomorphic to the image of f
questions.explanation: This fundamental theorem relates the quotient of the domain by the kernel to the image of the homomorphism.

questions.question: The set of integers ℤ under addition is an example of a group that is:
questions.correct_answer: Infinite and cyclic, generated by 1
questions.explanation: ℤ is cyclic because every integer is an integer multiple of the generator 1 (or −1), and it has infinitely many elements.

questions.question: What is the identity element of the group (ℤ_n, +) of integers modulo n under addition?
questions.explanation: Adding 0 to any element of ℤ_n leaves it unchanged modulo n, so 0 is the identity.

questions.question: In the group (ℤ_6, +), what is the order of the element 4?
questions.explanation: Adding 4 repeatedly modulo 6: 4, 4+4=8≡2, 2+4=6≡0, so 3×4≡0 (mod 6) and no smaller positive multiple of 4 is 0 mod 6, giving order 3.

questions.question: The direct product G × H of two groups G and H is a group whose elements are:
options: Ordered pairs (g, h) with g ∈ G, h ∈ H, with operation applied component-wise
The union of G and H
Only elements common to both G and H
The intersection of G and H
questions.correct_answer: Ordered pairs (g, h) with g ∈ G, h ∈ H, with operation applied component-wise
questions.explanation: The direct product combines two groups into a new group of ordered pairs, with the operation performed independently in each coordinate.

questions.question: Cayley's Theorem states that every group G is isomorphic to:
options: A subgroup of the symmetric group on the set G
questions.correct_answer: A subgroup of the symmetric group on the set G
questions.explanation: Cayley's Theorem shows every abstract group can be realized concretely as a group of permutations acting on itself.

questions.question: The center Z(G) of a group G is defined as:
options: {z ∈ G : zg = gz for all g ∈ G}
The set of all subgroups of G
questions.correct_answer: {z ∈ G : zg = gz for all g ∈ G}
questions.explanation: The center consists of elements that commute with every element of G, and it is always a normal subgroup of G.

questions.question: If G is an abelian group, then Z(G) equals:
questions.correct_answer: G itself
questions.explanation: In an abelian group every element commutes with every other, so the entire group equals its own center.
